headline: All seven majors sit under their 200-day lines, yet the crowd's longs are the ones getting liquidated
paragraphs: Start with regime, because it is unanimous today: every asset in the set, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, trades below its 200-day moving average, and none shows a golden cross. That is not a mixed picture, that is one direction across the board. The distance from 12-month highs tells you how far this stretch has run: BTC is 49.5% off its high, ETH 61.3%, SOL 70.6%, XRP 68.0%, BNB 55.7%, DOGE 75.9%, and ADA the furthest out at 82.0%. When every asset in a basket sits under trend by that much, you are not reading a dip, you are reading a market that has been in retreat for a while.

Momentum tells a more interesting story than trend does. RSI-14 readings cluster in the low-to-mid 40s and low 50s (BTC 45.1, ETH 51.1, SOL 42.0, XRP 41.7, BNB 52.7, DOGE 40.2, ADA 55.5), which is neither oversold nor overbought, just resting. MACD is where the split shows up: BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP sit below their signal lines, while BNB, DOGE, and ADA sit above. That is a real divergence worth naming, three of seven majors showing short-term momentum turning up even as price remains stuck under a falling 200-day average. Momentum flickering while trend stays negative is the kind of thing that shows up before either the trend catches down to the bounce, or the bounce fades back into the trend. The data does not say which.

Positioning adds texture. Long/short account ratios are long-heavy everywhere: BTC 2.08, ETH 2.2, SOL 2.67, XRP 3.18, DOGE 5.45. Funding, the periodic payment longs make to shorts (or vice versa) to keep a perpetual future tethered to spot, is positive and modest for BTC (2.5% annualized) and ETH (3.3%), hotter for SOL and DOGE (10.8% each), but negative for XRP (-11.1%), meaning XRP shorts are the ones paying today despite XRP having the most lopsided long account ratio in the set. Account count and funding cost are measuring different things, and here they disagree. Liquidations resolve some of the tension: over the past 22 to 24 hours, longs took the beating everywhere, BTC longs lost $8.48M against $352K in short liquidations, ETH $9.99M versus $952K, similar lopsided ratios in SOL, XRP, and DOGE. Crowded long positioning met a market that did not cooperate.

Flows are where the ETF tape needs care. BTC spot ETFs printed -$265.4M on 31 Jul, and the five-session net is also negative at -$61.5M, but same_direction_days reads 1, meaning only one of the last several sessions actually matched that outflow direction. That is a single loud day sitting on top of a choppier week, not a persistent trend. ETH ETFs printed +$9.0M on 31 Jul with a five-session net of +$10.0M and same_direction_days of 2, marginally more consistent but still thin. Whale activity over the last 24 hours shows zero net value moving off exchanges, flat, with the one notable transfer being $100.86M in USDT moving onto Bitfinex, stablecoin buying power arriving rather than coins leaving. Zoom out to the weekly net figures and the last four readings alternate: +$720.3M, -$279.9M, +$380.9M, +$906.3M, mostly net outflow from exchanges on a weekly view even as today sits flat. Stablecoin float itself is down 1.64% over 30 days to $303.89B, dry powder contracting slightly even as fresh USDT lands on an exchange today.

Sentiment sits at Fear, 27, inside its own 30-day range of 20 to 33, so this is fear near the low end of its recent band, not a fresh extreme. It lines up with the trend picture (seven majors under the 200-day) but sits oddly against today's price action, where BTC and ETH both ticked green (+0.31% and +0.23%) and ADA jumped 2.93%. The crowd feels the multi-month damage more than the day's tape shows. What is worth watching from here: whether the MACD crossovers in BNB, DOGE, and ADA spread to the rest of the set or fade, whether BTC ETF flows string together more than one same-direction day, and whether that weekly whale outflow pattern turns into a same-direction stretch rather than the alternating sign it shows now.
